state:
Goal `tools-config`. Five of the configuration chapter's features have all their proofs:
`app-per-application-blocks`, `auditing-a-tree`, `capabilities`, `network-grants-the-addresses-and-endpoints-they-reach`
and `include-a-tree-of-files` (each `tools:config/<slug>`). A tool feature owes one example, one attack and one
test (Rust with a `covers:` marker counts); `bun nv proofs --id '<feature>'` says so, and adds `help` when its
reference section shows no code. A feature whose example needs settings puts its own `nvs.toml` in the feature
directory (`docs/examples/README.md` § *A grant the examples need*), and `bun nv try` copies a script away from
it, so run such a proof with `bun nv proofs --run --show --id '<feature>'`. A `[limits]` key with no
`[limits.hard]` entry has no ceiling, so an attack on `Core\Config::set` writes the ceiling it tests.
Nothing is blocked.

next.title: the dossier, file order
next.note: one file set: `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md` and the `docs/examples/tools/config/`, `tests/hostile/tools/config/` trees, each with its own `nvs.toml`.

items.text: **`tools:config/trust`** — owes examples, hostile, tests and `help`. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md:396` shows no code: add a short block of how a trusted tree is written, which `nvs agent show` then prints. `nvs run` does not apply the `E0607` check (the section says so), so the example and the attack show what a program can and cannot do to its own tree, not the refusal.

**`tools:config/secrets-from-files`** — owes examples, hostile, tests. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md:409`. `[db.<name>] password_file` and `[mail.<name>] password_file` are the two pairs; a Rust test in `crates/nvs-config/tests/` may take the `covers:` marker.

**`tools:config/reading-and-changing-it-from-a-program-core-config`** — owes examples, hostile, tests. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md:472`. The attacks under `tests/hostile/tools/config/capabilities/` and `include-a-tree-of-files/` already call `Core\Config::set`; this one attacks `get` and `set` themselves.

backlog: `[storage.<disk>] root` resolves against the working directory, and `rule:config/a-relative-path-resolves-against-the-file-it-is-written-in` says every path-valued directive resolves against its file; not checked where the storage root is read. Moving it rewrites the `Storage` proofs' `nvs.toml` roots.
